Ajustes.Propiedad.OptimizeStatsOnLegaliz: After legalizing, raises IVs as far as the encounter allows. On by default. Does not change origin data or break legality: if optimizing would make the Pokémon invalid, the valid result is applied without optimization.
Ajustes.Propiedad.CoherentHistory.Descri: Pokémon created by Pokekeep have a believable history: only ribbons from their origin, real dates and no unrelated previous Trainer. Never breaks legality. “Optimize stats” does not change this history.
Ajustes.Propiedad.LegalizeTimeoutSeconds: Maximum search time for “Legalize automatically” and “Add to box”. When it runs out, “Timed out” is shown; this does not prove the result is impossible. Between 10 and 3600 seconds.
Ajustes.Propiedad.OptimizeTimeoutSeconds: Time limit for “Optimize stats”. Exhaustively searching seeds for some encounters (raids, Legends) can take a couple of minutes. Between 10 and 3600 seconds.
Ajustes.Propiedad.AllowHomeTrackerless.D: Off by default. RISK: without the tracker assigned by Pokémon HOME, PKHeX considers the Pokémon invalid until you transfer it through HOME. Pokekeep cannot check how Nintendo’s servers or the games will handle it. Never invents a tracker. Affects Pokémon GO transfers to Switch, HOME gifts and some evolutions and forms; the summary warns “Needs to pass through HOME”.
Ajustes.Propiedad.BulkWorkers.Descripcio: How many engine processes work at once for “Complete the game” and “Bulk edit”. Between 1 and 8. Defaults to half the CPU cores (up to 4).
Ajustes.Propiedad.LivingDexForms.Descrip: Which forms “Complete the game” generates: one per species (default), all storable forms, or one per species plus regional forms.
Ajustes.Propiedad.LivingDexOrder.Descrip: Box order for “Complete the game”: National Pokédex (default), or the game’s regional Pokédex when PKHeX knows it.
Ajustes.Propiedad.LivingDexSkipOwned.Des: Skips a species and form if you already have a legal Pokémon of that species and form in your boxes or party. On by default.
Ajustes.Propiedad.PreferEventVersion.Des: Off by default. In “Complete the game”, Legendary, sub-Legendary and Mythical Pokémon are first attempted from a legal event card. The fixed order favors cards that do not require HOME, then Spanish-language cards, European distributions, guaranteed shininess, cards restricted to one language and older distributions. Changing the interface language does not change this order. If no card produces a legal result, the usual origin is used. PKHeX decides legality.
Ajustes.Propiedad.RegisterInPokedex.Desc: When adding a Pokémon from the Library or with “Complete the game”, marks it as seen and caught in the save’s Pokédex, as when you obtain it in the game. Uses PKHeX’s registration logic; does not change the Pokémon or its legality. On by default. “Undo” restores the Pokémon but does not remove the Pokédex registration.
Ajustes.Propiedad.ShowSummary.Descripcio: Shows the summary bar with “View changes” and “Undo” when an operation finishes. Failures are always shown.
Ajustes.Propiedad.SmoothBoxSprites.Descr: Off by default: box Pokémon are drawn as in PKHeX, pixel by pixel at an integer scale. When on, a pixel art scaler rounds corners and diagonals without blurring. Presentation only: does not change any data. Uses a little more memory when browsing boxes.

GuiaGuardados.AplicarGuardaBorradorSesio: Apply stores the draft in the session with Undo. Save verifies the original document and makes a backup; Export copy creates another file. Back closes sheets and editors first and asks if there are pending changes. Don’t uninstall the app to install an update: you would lose its private data.
GuiaGuardados.AplicarCambiaSesionGuardar: Apply changes the session; Save changes the file
GuiaGuardados.TocaValorEscribirAbrir: Select the value to type or open the picker; the field menu offers the available actions. Use the editor’s IV, EV, PID, ID and shiny buttons. The limit depends on the Pokémon’s format; not every game has the same fields.
GuiaGuardados.MantenPulsadoSeleccionarVa: Press and hold to select several. In the slot menu choose Move or Copy and then select the destination. The box menu offers the scope, All boxes and Reverse when they apply. Check the scope shown before sorting, deleting or running a batch.
GuiaGuardados.TocaCasillaVerFicha: Select a slot to see its summary and its ⋮ menu. Edit opens the fields; View legality shows the report; Legalize automatically and Optimize stats run Pokekeep’s actions. The sprite follows the style of the save.
GuiaGuardados.PCUsaMenuEmulador: On PC, use the emulator’s menu to find the saves folder. On Android, each app chooses its own location; if it doesn’t show up in the picker, export from the emulator to Downloads or share it with Pokekeep. Android restricts private folders: Pokekeep doesn’t force that access. Open the loose file, check the game and Trainer, and use Export copy to go back to the emulator. If the file you received is read-only, Save can’t replace it.
GuiaGuardados.ArchivoAccesibleDesdeSelec: File reachable from the system picker
GuiaGuardados.DondeGuardadoAndroidCopias: Where is my save? · Android and PC copies
GuiaGuardados.ArchivoPokemonPartidaAbre: A Pokémon file is not a save. Open the destination save first and then the Pokémon, to edit it or put it in a box. A .pkh holds one HOME entity, not your account or all its boxes. Pokekeep doesn’t sign in to HOME or modify server data. Dumps and rental teams are recognized by their content; importing them depends on the format and game that are open.
GuiaGuardados.PokemonHOMEPokemonIndividu: Pokémon HOME, single Pokémon and boxes
GuiaGuardados.DolphinPuedeGuardarGameCub: Dolphin can save GameCube games on a card or in a folder of GCI files. On PC, use its card manager to extract the Colosseum or XD save if you need to. Pokekeep also recognizes whole cards and asks which game to open. Battle Revolution holds several profiles: choose the save under Save. Don’t replace a whole card with a GCI file.
GuiaGuardados.ExportaGuardadoJuegoDesde: Export the game’s save from the emulator; the extension depends on how it stores cartridge memory. Copy the file to your phone and open it in Pokekeep. Recognition uses its data, so changing an extension isn’t enough. When you go back to the emulator, keep the name it expects. In RetroArch, check Settings > Directory to find your install’s saves folder.
GuiaGuardados.GuardaDesdeMenuJuego: Save from the game’s menu. DeSmuME offers File > Export Backup Memory to get a .sav; .dsv is also a recognized format. In other emulators, identify the save memory copy next to the game or through its export. A save state holds the machine’s state and is not the file Pokekeep asks for.
GuiaGuardados.LocalizaGuardadoTituloUsua: Find the save of the title and the active user in the emulator. On PC, the save location menu saves you from guessing paths; on Android, export the save if the folder is private. Extract the copy before opening it. BDSP uses SaveData.bin; don’t rename every game to main. After editing, import the copy exported by Pokekeep with the game closed.
GuiaGuardados.MainSaveDataBinU: main · SaveData.bin or another name depending on the game
GuiaGuardados.EmuladorPCAbreUbicacion: On a PC emulator, open the game’s save location or use its export. On Android, use the data/save export your version offers and extract the game’s file. Don’t choose a ROM, an install file or the whole sdmc folder. Menu names and the folder change between versions: use the right game and profile.
GuiaGuardados.GuardaDentroJuegoCierralo: Save inside the game, close it and export a copy. Open that copy with Pokekeep’s folder button. Emulator save states don’t replace the game’s own save.
